points.why: It names Goodhart's law and contrasts the measured proxy (tickets closed without escalation) with the real goal of solving customers' problems.
It covers the quick metric win, the delayed and unmeasured damage (slow churn signal, abandonment) and why retraining would intensify the harm, without naming the archetype.
It recommends outcome measures (customer-confirmed resolution, reopen rate, CSAT, churn comparisons), early-warning signals to shorten the delay, and not chasing the proxy.
It critiques the target and escalation-avoidance but never states the 'no escalation means solved' belief outright or asks who set the goal.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly argues against retraining for a higher number.
It frames the problem as the objective and measurement, not a broken model.
